newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk union says boycott hitting oil giants' sales.
newsitem.headline: Turk union says boycott hitting oil giants' sales.

text.p: Turkey's petrochemical industry workers' union said on Thursday it estimated that a boycott of oil giants Shell, BP and Mobil was cutting their sales a total 1.5 trillion Turkish lira ($15.4 million) a month.

The protest, which began in July, targets the products of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, British Petroleum Co Plc and Mobil Corp because the companies refuse to recognise union rights, the Petrol-Is union said.

"According to our rough estimates approaching 150,000 car owners and around 100 organisations are consciously not buying the products of these companies," Petrol-Is general secretary Mansur Burgucu said in a statement.
"The sales of these three companies can be calculated to have fallen 1.5 trillion lira a month," he said.

A spokeswoman at BP in Turkey said the boycott was not having an impact on sales. "This boycott is certainly unfair, but it's not effecting our sales," external affairs manager at BP in Turkey, Deniz Guzeloz, told Reuters.
Spokespersons at Mobil and Shell in Turkey were not immediately available for comment.
Union confederations, professional and industry associations were represented at a meeting on Thursday to discuss the broadening of the campaign, Petrol-Is said.

"The de-unionisation standpoint of these companies is against several laws in Turkey and is contrary to international agreements, notably those of the ILO (International Labour Organisation)," Burgucu said.
He said a committee will co-ordinate the distribution of leaflets, collecting signatures in support of the campaign's demands and visits to organisations to persuade them to join the boycott.
